Header:
Date: 2025-02-19
Time: 03:00 PM PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (NovaHealth ML), Marta Gomez (NovaHealth PM), Tony Ruiz (Head of Security), Elena Park (Data Scientist)
Recording ID: fireflies-20250219-7a9c

Summary:
- Reviewed weekly quality eval for the pilot (week 3).
- Found a small regression on the "billing extraction" prompt cluster after applying a new prompt template; overall latency and cost within expected range on hosted model variant but customer wants Dedicated cost projection.
- Discussed guardrails: additional prefixing, post-hoc classifier, KMS and audit log needs for Private option.
- Agreed next steps: run regression with updated prompt set + quantized model, customer to provide extra edge-case prompts, Redwood to share SOW + pricing.

Topics Covered:
- Evaluation metrics and scoring methodology (human/auto hybrid)
- Prompt sets and regression detection
- Guardrails and safety filters (toxicity, PII filters)
- Hosting options and encryption/KMS requirements
- Next steps and owners

Action Items (recorded in notes):
- Priya: run detailed regression & per-prompt breakdown (24h job)
- Jordan: supply extra eval cases
- Alex: send pricing + SOW
- Tony: confirm security/KMS checklist items

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: okay, uh thanks everyone for joining, we should be able to keep this to about 40 minutes, i'm alex from Redwood, i own the pilot, and with me is priya and samir.
[00:18] Priya Singh: hey everyone, hi, hi, hi. i'll be running the quality and regression checks this week, quick note — i pushed the updated prompt templates to the shared sheet last night, link in the chat.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: got it, saw the note. quick question — are we still testing on the hosted variant or did you flip to the quantized model for the reg checks?
[00:45] Priya Singh: good question. for week 3 i ran the new prompt templates on hosted r-inference default, and a separate pass on the 4-bit quantized variant on dedicated hardware to estimate cost — results are in the sheet.
[01:02] Marta Gomez: quick context for the group: we're most worried about false positives in billing extraction, that causes manual review and drives us nuts. anything that increases FP is a blocker for rollout.
[01:18] Priya Singh: yep, that's consistent with what we saw. overall F1 is stable at ~0.87, but the billing cluster dropped from 0.92 to 0.84 after the prompt template change, looks like the prompt rephrasing traded precision for recall in edge cases.
[01:41] Jordan Lee: that matches our observations in the app — we saw more spurious extractions on invoices with header footers, maybe the new system prompt is too permissive.
[01:55] Alex Mercer: do you know if those invoices are multi-language or have scanned OCR artifacts? sometimes OCR noise causes tokenization weirdness, we can pre-clean or add a short instruction to ignore bad OCR.
[02:12] Elena Park: majority are english but 12% are spanish, and yes OCR noise — the ocr pipeline sometimes inserts weird hyphens and line breaks.
[02:26] Priya Singh: okay, quick plan — i'll run a targeted regression focusing on the billing prompt cluster with two variants: 1) revert to prior prompt template, 2) keep new template + add a strict preface "only extract numerical billing lines, ignore headers" — we'll compare precision/recall.
[02:47] Jordan Lee: sounds good. also can you include token counts and latency distribution? when we looked at the dedicated 4-bit run latency was slightly better but there were tails at ~450ms for some requests.
[03:02] Priya Singh: yes, i'll include P50/P95/P99 and token cost. initial hosted runs had avg latency 220ms, dedicated quantized had avg 180ms but p99 bumped up on long sequences.
[03:21] Tony Ruiz: from security side we need to know what gets logged — is KV cache stored in plaintext in logs? we need auditability but also encryption.
[03:33] Priya Singh: good call — the platform by default logs request metadata and model variant, not full payloads, but for the pilot we can toggle full transcript logging. for Private we support KMS/HSM integration to encrypt at rest and provide audit logs.
[03:50] Tony Ruiz: and SSO/SAML support? we have to map RBAC to our internal groups.
[03:57] Alex Mercer: yes, we have SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC roles map to your AD groups, and we can share the security pack — i'll send SOC2 artifacts.
[04:12] Marta Gomez: on compliance, are backups geo-redundant? we have data residency needs for EU customers.
[04:20] Priya Singh: hosted uses regional storage, dedicated can be pinned to region, private on-prem is obviously controlled by you — we'll add a column in the SOW about region pinning.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: coming back to quality, how are you detecting regressions automatically? do you run per-prompt scoring and alert on drift?
[04:46] Priya Singh: yes, we run nightly evals on the canonical prompt set; if any prompt cluster drops >3% absolute in F1 or shows >5% increase in false positives, it triggers a regression alert and pins the rollout. this week the billing cluster hit a 4-pt drop.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: can you show us the per-prompt breakdown now?
[05:09] Priya Singh: sure — um i'm pulling the sheet, on screen share you'll see the cluster table; billing cluster has 120 samples, precision moved from 0.95 to 0.88, recall went 0.89 to 0.80. (audio: brief typing)
[05:35] Marta Gomez: okay that explains the spike in manual reviews. do you have examples of false positives?
[05:42] Priya Singh: yes — see examples column: invoice #s picked up from headers, totals from bank account lines, stuff that looks like amounts but are actually ref numbers. i'll include the raw utterances in the exports.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: is there an easy guardrail like a post-classifier to filter extractions with low confidence?
[06:05] Priya Singh: absolutely — two quick options: add a downstream threshold classifier (lightweight) or add prompt-level constraints + canonicalization step. we can run both and compare FP reduction vs added latency.
[06:20] Alex Mercer: also we can enable prefix-based guardrails: a strict system instruction to only extract amounts that match regex X and adjacent context Y — that often buys back precision.
[06:32] Elena Park: regex helps but we still need to catch OCR errors where decimals are comma or spaces inserted.
[06:40] Priya Singh: noted — we'll add normalization pre-step in the pipeline.
[06:46] Jordan Lee: any changes in hallucination or toxicity flags after the prompt tweaks?
[06:52] Priya Singh: no significant toxicity shifts; hallucination rate on generative summaries is flat. for extraction tasks we saw the FP increase I described.
[07:04] Marta Gomez: cost — you mentioned dedicated estimates, can you summarize?
[07:09] Priya Singh: sure — high level: hosted pilot cost was about $0.005/token effective after caching; the dedicated 4-bit estimate reduces unit cost by ~30% for steady throughput but requires a monthly reserved capacity commitment; i'll attach a computed table in the follow-up.
[07:28] Alex Mercer: and we can do a hybrid — keep low-latency endpoints on hosted for customer-facing flows, move batch heavy jobs to dedicated.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: that hybrid sounds promising, need numbers though.
[07:40] Alex Mercer: we'll include a cost/capacity spreadsheet.
[07:44] Tony Ruiz: back to security item — what about key management: does the Redwood private offer let us bring our own KMS?
[07:50] Priya Singh: yes BYOK with HSM support for the Private option and KMS integration for Dedicated; hosted offers provider-managed encryption but we can do customer-managed keys for enterprise customers.
[08:03] Tony Ruiz: good. also need to ensure audit logs are tamper-evident and retained for 12 months.
[08:11] Samir Patel: noted, we'll include retention SLA options in the SOW.
[08:16] Jordan Lee: one more question — when you run the regression job, will you run cross-model comparisons? like original hosted, quantized dedicated and a fallback smaller model?
[08:27] Priya Singh: yes, we'll run baseline, quantized 4-bit, and a smaller fast model for fallback. the pipeline will output per-model confusion matrices.
[08:38] Marta Gomez: that will help decide fallback policies for production.
[08:42] Priya Singh: on the guardrail side i also recommend post-hoc deterministic checks before write-back to your database — that can be a quick safety net.
[08:53] Jordan Lee: agreed.
[08:56] Alex Mercer: okay, let's go through the concrete next steps and owners. priya — regression + per-prompt breakdown (include P50/P95/P99, tokens, example false positives); jordan — provide 30 extra edge-case prompts; alex — SOW and pricing; tony — security checklist.
[09:14] Jordan Lee: timeline ok: we can get the prompts by monday.
[09:19] Tony Ruiz: security notes i can send by friday.
[09:23] Alex Mercer: great. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time unless something comes up.
[09:29] Priya Singh: quick nit — for regression alerts do you want slack notifications or email?
[09:34] Jordan Lee: slack is better, can we get channel + thread with automated summary?
[09:38] Priya Singh: yes we can wire a regression webhook to slack and post daily summaries + links to detailed report.
[09:45] Alex Mercer: anything else on quality or regressions?
[09:48] Marta Gomez: one ask — can you add a column for "business impact" in the export so stakeholders see severity?
[09:55] Priya Singh: yep i'll add business impact tags (high/med/low) and estimated weekly manual reviews avoided metric.
[10:03] Alex Mercer: awesome — wrap up, recap next steps.
[10:08] Alex Mercer: recap: Priya run regression + guardrail experiments; Alex send SOW/pricing + security pack; Jordan deliver extra eval prompts; Tony deliver security/KMS requirements. next meeting tuesday 2025-02-25 3pm PST.
[10:25] Marta Gomez: thanks, bye.
[10:27] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone.
[10:30] End of recording
